channel.title: Aunmoy Dey Tanmoy — Engineering Notes
channel.description: Articles on Go, backend systems and distributed architecture.

item.title: "Hello, World" is Not a Demo: The First Service as Your Platform's Operating Model
item.description: Discover how to build a production-grade Golden Path for AI-ready Go microservices using Kubernetes, Helm, and GitOps to streamline platform engineering.

item.title: Why Use a Buffered Channel? Worker Pools & Batch Aggregation in Go
item.description: A deep dive into Go's buffered channels, showing how worker pools, backpressure, and atomic database flushes are implemented in production.

item.title: High-Concurrency DAG Execution Engine: Architecture & Design
item.description: A deep technical dive into building a distributed DAG execution engine, covering scheduling, state consensus, idempotency, backpressure, and fault tolerance.

item.title: How Netflix, OpenAI, and Uber Orchestrate Millions of Tasks in Seconds
item.description: Explore the power of Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) execution engines to automate and parallelize complex, dependency-aware task graphs at scale.

item.title: Caching High-Level Design: Strategies, Layers, and Trade-offs
item.description: A comprehensive guide to caching in distributed systems, covering external caching with Redis, in-process caching, CDNs, and client-side strategies.

item.title: Event-Driven Architecture (HLD): Saga Pattern, Outbox Pattern & CQRS
item.description: A deep dive into Event-Driven Architecture (EDA) for high-scale distributed systems. Learn how to implement Saga workflows, the Transactional Outbox pattern, and CQRS.

item.title: Kubernetes from the Ground Up: A Senior Engineer's Deep Dive
item.description: Master Kubernetes internals - from control plane scheduling and container runtimes to resource limits, cgroups, and rolling updates.

item.title: Dependency Inversion Principle (DIP) in Go: Writing Loose, Testable Code
item.description: Learn how to implement the Dependency Inversion Principle in Go, mapping abstractions to interfaces to decouple high-level logic from low-level details.

item.title: Liskov Substitution Principle (LSP) in Go & Distributed Systems
item.description: How the Liskov Substitution Principle translates to Go's implicit interfaces and distributed architectures, ensuring behavioral contracts aren't broken.

item.title: Object-Oriented Programming in Go: Pragmatic LLD Patterns
item.description: Go doesn't have classes, but it has package-level encapsulation, interface composition, and method attachment. Let's explore pragmatic OOP in Go.

item.title: Scalability High-Level Design: Database Sharding, Replication & Load Balancing
item.description: A senior engineer's guide to scalability, sharding keys, database replication, horizontal scaling, and cost-efficient scheduling.
